ONE SMALL DETAIL. A BIG DIFFERENCE.

The darkest color
gets the background.

Every original scheme pins the source palette’s darkest color as its terminal background, measured by relative luminance. Even when that color is electric indigo.

Original palette values stay intact. Extra ANSI shades are derived as needed. Preview each scheme and check foreground contrast before choosing.

Will this replace my settings.json?

The installer builds and validates a merged candidate, backs up the original, then replaces the file atomically. It inserts only the missing schemes and preserves unrelated settings and JSONC comments. If validation fails, the candidate is not written.

How do I restore the original settings?

Close any open settings editor and copy the timestamped settings.json.backup-… file over your settings.json. Full instructions are in the bundle README.

Can I add JSON palettes from another repository?

Yes. Place supported JSON files under palettes/ and run python scripts/Sync-PaletteCatalog.py. The scanner recognizes creative collections, named color maps, hex arrays and Windows Terminal scheme collections. It adds provenance and does not modify source files. New non-terminal palettes are shown without inventing ready-to-install terminal schemes.

Which repository palettes are included?

This release contains the 10 recovered creative palettes and their corresponding Terminal schemes. No additional remote repository data was accessible during this build. The repository package contains a scanner for incorporating it later. GitHub publication is awaiting authenticated repository access; the product page is deployed separately.
